title: "DIANA AND THE MAIDENS" FAN AND CASE
medium: Paper, ivory, mother-of-pearl, copper alloy; opaque watercolor and gold paint, and selectively applied glaze, carved, incised, and gilded sticks and guards, pivot, rivet
medium_parts: opaque watercolor and gold paint, and selectively applied glaze, carved, incised, and gilded sticks and guards, pivot, rivet
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Floyd F. Reighley
identifying_description: Leaf of paper with opaque watercolor, gold paint, and selectively applied glaze showing scene of Diana and huntresses. On reverse, painted scene of Minerva in battle dress. Sticks and guards of carved, incised, and gilded ivory with chinoiserie designs. Mother-of-pearl pivot; and copper alloy rivet.
web_text: Idyllic countrysides frequently served as backdrops in eighteenth-century fan designs, reflecting urban society's idealization of the pastoral. These landscapes were well-suited settings for both romantic scenes and mythological tales. In this example, Diana, Roman goddess of the hunt, is shown at center, flanked by her attendants. Their bows, arrows, and quivers are cast aside as they enjoy nature's bounty. Typical for representations of Diana, she wears a crescent moon on her head and is accompanied by two hunting dogs, shown at the far left.
